output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses is most likely caused by the 12 August relay server move, not by agency nurses. The new server imported only 3 of the 14 forwarding rules. It lost the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, the 60-second suppression of repeat alerts, and the routing of probe-off and leads-off alarms to the charge phone only. The import tool logged a warning but reported success. Pod D was still on the old server. Since 12 August, Pods A-C nurses get about 80 phone notifications per shift, up from about 38. Their acknowledgement time doubled. Pod D is unchanged. Delayed responses in Pods A-C rose about fourfold for core, agency and agency-equivalent staff alike. Pod D agency share is similar and Pod D incidents did not rise. The raw alarm rate from the monitors did not change, including after the 23-24 September software update. So acuity and the update are not the cause. Higher sick leave may be a consequence of the alarm load, but that link is not proven. Do not cap agency use or open performance reviews. Do not switch off phone alarms. Restore the 11 skipped rules with clinical validation, then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Confidence is high. The Room 14 reports of phones not ringing should be checked separately.
